Compare SVG statistics across multiple gene sets

Source: R/svg_gene_set.R
plot_svg_gene_sets.Rd

Plot distributions of spatial variability statistics for multiple user-defined gene sets across normalisation methods.

Usage

plot_svg_gene_sets(
  svg_norm,
  gene_sets,
  stat = "LR_stat",
  method_order = NULL,
  method_colors = NULL,
  gene_id = "rownames",
  transform = c("log1p", "log", "none"),
  plot_type = c("boxplot", "violin"),
  scales = c("free_y", "fixed", "free"),
  facet_ncol = 2,
  add_jitter = TRUE,
  point_size = 1,
  alpha = 0.65,
  jitter_alpha = 0.5,
  box_width = 0.65,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  x_label = "Normalisation method",
  y_label = NULL,
  show_legend = FALSE,
  theme_name = "classic"
)

Arguments

svg_norm

Named list of SVG results.

gene_sets

Named list of character vectors containing genes for each gene set.

stat

SVG statistic. Default is "LR_stat".

method_order

Optional normalisation method order.

method_colors

Optional named vector of method colours.

gene_id

Gene identifier.

transform

Transformation: "log1p", "log", or "none".

plot_type

Plot type: "boxplot" or "violin".

scales

Facet scales: "fixed", "free_y", or "free".

facet_ncol

Number of facet columns.

add_jitter

Logical. Display individual gene points.

point_size

Size of jittered points.

alpha

Transparency of boxplots or violins.

jitter_alpha

Transparency of jittered points.

box_width

Width of boxplots.

title

Optional plot title.

subtitle

Optional plot subtitle.

x_label

X-axis label.

y_label

Optional y-axis label.

show_legend

Logical. Display method legend.

theme_name

Plot theme.

Value

List containing plotting data and ggplot.

Details

Gene sets may include housekeeping genes, negative-control genes, biological marker genes, or any custom gene sets.

Each gene set is displayed in a separate facet.

Examples

data(svg_example)

marker_genes <- head(rownames(svg_example[[1]]), 5)

p <- plot_svg_stat(
  svg_norm = svg_example,
  genes = marker_genes,
  stat = "LR_stat",
  transform = "log"
)

p$plot
